note: Held-out set for D11, written 2026-10-17 BEFORE incident prompt v3 existed. Question: does the incident agent type aftermath and preparation reports with the right disaster type (so that the knowledge base is searched), without typing non-disaster reports as a disaster? REVISION, committed before v3 existed: the first baseline of v2 (eval/results/incident_type_check/20261017-230810) showed that v2 already types aftermath reports correctly (h01 to h06) and fails on preparation reports (h07, h08 typed unclear) and on n01 (a car through a shop window typed structural_emergency). h07, h08 and n01 are therefore seen cases; h09 to h12 and n07 to n10 were added as fresh cases. Revised pass criteria (v3 against v2, same pinned model, 2 runs, calls that returned an error are excluded and counted separately): (1) on the fresh positives h09 to h12, v3 is correct in at least 7 of 8 answered runs; (2) no negative (n01 to n10) is typed forest_fire, flood or structural in any answered run of v3; (3) the six fixed incidents keep their expected type in every answered run; (4) v3 is not worse than v2 on h01 to h06. If (2), (3) or (4) fail, v3 is not adopted whatever it does on (1). Results on the seen cases h07, h08, n01 are reported but are not evidence of generalisation.

L'incendie de forêt est éteint mais il reste des braises. Les habitants veulent rentrer chez eux ce soir.
The flood has gone down but our house is full of mud and the walls are wet. How do we clean it safely?
L'eau s'est retirée après la crue. Nous rentrons chez nous et il y a des fils électriques par terre.
The earthquake is over. Our apartment block has cracks in the walls and an inspector put a yellow sign on the door. Can we stay?
Après l'explosion, des morceaux du balcon menacent de tomber sur la rue. Que doit faire la mairie ?
We live next to a pine forest. What should we do to protect our house before the fire season?
Nous vivons près d'un oued. Comment préparer la famille avant la saison des pluies ?
